**The Last Letter**

I found it tucked between the pages of an old, yellowed novel—*The Shadow of the Wind* by Carlos Ruiz Zafón, though I’m not sure if that’s where it was originally. The letter was crumpled, the edges frayed, and the ink had bled into the paper like a slow, inevitable stain.

*Dear [Name],*

I hope this letter finds you well, though I know it’s unlikely. I’ve been thinking about you for years, ever since that night in the café when you smiled at me and I nearly dropped my coffee. You were reading *The Stranger* by Camus, and I was reading *The Metamorphosis*—we both looked up at the same moment, and for a second, the world stopped.

I don’t know why I’m writing this now. Maybe because I’m leaving town. Maybe because I’ve finally decided to face the things I’ve been running from. Or maybe because I’ve realized that some letters are meant to be written, even if they’re never sent.

I don’t know what you’re doing now. I don’t know if you remember me. But if you ever read this, I hope it doesn’t make you feel bad. I hope it makes you smile, even if it’s just for a moment.

I’ll leave you with a quote from *The Stranger*:

*"The struggle itself toward the heights is enough to fill a man’s heart."*

That’s what I’ve been trying to do—struggle, even if it’s just to keep going.

Take care of yourself.

*—[Name]*

I folded the letter carefully, pressed it into my pocket, and walked away. The novel was still there, open to the same page, as if waiting for me to continue the story. But I didn’t. I just walked, and the wind carried the scent of rain and old books with it.
